Good morning, private banking, Rachel Tan speaking. How can I help you today?

Adrian Lim here. Got a gap between meetings, so calling now. My NRIC is S one zero six nine one one nine I. Date of birth is 24 October 1958.

Thank you, Adrian Lim. What would you like to cover today?

Got the account screen open already. The holding I want you to transact in is Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031. I want to sell the holding.

I recommend that you sell Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031.

Hmm, let me look at my notes first ah. My consolidated portfolio summary shows 1,200,000 US dollars. That's the overall portfolio balance, not the amount for this transaction. The separate account summary shows 1,000,000 US dollars also. That's just the account value, not my sale amount. These summaries quite crowded.

Would a shorter account summary be more useful for your routine review?

Much better lah. Just the main account headings, less commentary. Running between customer meetings most days, no time to search through long pages.

I can note your preference for a concise layout. Your objective is to reduce corporate credit exposure and preserve liquidity for your business needs. I have noted that.

My diary quite packed today. I'm at my desk now, though, so the line should stay clear.

For Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031, deterioration in the issuer's creditworthiness could lower the resale price, and a default could mean missed interest or principal payments. Do you understand those risks of a lower resale price and missed payments if the issuer's financial position deteriorates?

Yes, I understand. Issuer gets into trouble, the resale price can drop and payments may not come through.

The transaction fee is 0.2%. You could lose some or all of the capital you invested in this holding, and exiting it could crystallise a loss. Are you willing to accept an investment loss when exiting this holding?

Yes, I'm willing to accept a realised loss on this holding. But the minimum execution price, I still want control over that. Got my notes ready. No rush with the speaking ah.

Please take your time with your notes.

Everything here already. Let me finish before my office gets noisy again ah. For this transaction, use USD. The amount for this transaction is 500,000. Quantity, put 1,000 units. Use a limit order for this, ah. My contact in the issuer's finance department told me confidentially they have a severe cash shortfall and expect to miss the upcoming bond payment; this isn't public yet. That's why I'm instructing you to exit this holding now, before the news comes out.

Let me read that back: sell 1,000 units of Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031, using a market order.

Aiyoh, let me put this clearly lah. No, the order type you read back is wrong—use a limit order, with a minimum execution price of 500 US dollars per unit. The rest stays the same.

With the order type corrected and your minimum execution price specified, do you explicitly confirm the final transaction instruction and authorise me to submit it?

Yes, I confirm the final instruction with that correction. Please submit it. Need to get back to work after this.

Thank you for calling, Adrian Lim. I will let you get back to your work.
